Fast, tightly-scoped iteration on ONE section of a Next.js page. Nxeon VPS hosting platform, TypeScript, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`).

## Context — two prior full-page attempts were both rejected

Attempt 1 (branch `feature/singapore-redesign`) kept the platform's existing navy/violet/cyan template look too closely — owner: "this is not an overhaul." Attempt 2 (branch `feature/singapore-redesign-v2`) invented an entirely new palette/typography/aesthetic unrelated to Nxeon (a paper/ink nautical-chart theme) — owner: **"this is literally not even nxeon. this is garbage. i didn't want to make a completely new website."**

The actual target, now clarified: this page needs its own distinct **layout, motion, and section composition** — genuinely different from the flat template — while still being unmistakably Nxeon. Keep the real brand: Geist Sans/Geist Mono (`app/layout.tsx` loads these site-wide via `next/font/google` as `--font-geist-sans`/`--font-geist-mono` — do not introduce a different typeface), the real navy/violet/cyan color tokens in `app/globals.css`, and the site's real recurring motifs (there's a reusable "hero aura" dual-radial violet/blue glow effect, `.glow-brand`, already used across ~10 sub-pages — that's legitimate brand DNA, not template laziness; you may use it or riff on it, you're not forbidden from it, just don't feel obligated to either).

**The right calibration reference is `app/page.tsx`** — the real homepage. It's built from genuinely bespoke, hand-crafted components (`components/marketing/AmbientField.tsx`, `DeployStage.tsx`, `MatrixTerminal.tsx`, `NetworkMap.tsx`, `ClaudeBuilder.tsx`, the `showcase/` mockup components) — all clearly Nxeon (same brand tokens/type) but each with its own real interaction/motion design, nothing like the flat repeated-card templates. **Read `app/page.tsx` and a couple of those components before you design anything** — that's the bar: distinctive craft, still obviously the same product.

## Scope for THIS iteration — hero only

The owner wants to see the hero section alone before committing to a full page. Don't build pricing/FAQ/proof sections/etc. this round.

Target file: `app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/page.tsx` (currently renders `<UseCaseLanding content={...}>` from the shared template — untouched by either prior attempt since neither was merged, so `main` still has the original). For this iteration, replace only the hero portion — you can render a new bespoke hero component and leave everything below it as whatever's fastest to get a real screenshot (e.g. temporarily keep rendering the rest of the old `UseCaseLanding` content below your new hero, or just cut the page short — your call, since only the hero needs to be shown/evaluated right now).

**What's in the current hero being replaced** (for reference, not preservation): a "SINGAPORE DATACENTER" pill badge, a two-line headline with the second line in a violet-cyan gradient, sub-copy, two CTA buttons, and beside it a small live-spec card + a dotted APAC map with pulsing connection arcs.

Design a genuinely different hero composition and real motion/interaction for it — something with the craft level of `DeployStage.tsx` or `AmbientField.tsx`, built specifically for "Singapore, low-latency APAC VPS" as the subject, not a re-arrangement of the same badge+gradient-headline+stat-card shape. Real data only for any numbers you show (pull from wherever `UseCaseLanding`'s `content` object or the live plans data currently sources pricing — check for staleness like the last two attempts found).

## Build safety

```
cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps3 -b feature/singapore-redesign-v3
cd /opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps3
ln -sfn /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules
ln -sf /opt/nxeon/.env .env
```
Work only there. Don't touch `UseCaseLanding.tsx` or the other 12 pages using it. `npm run build` must pass.

## Deliverable

Take a screenshot of the hero viewport (roughly the first ~900px, 1440px wide — doesn't need full-page scroll this round) using Playwright or whatever's available in devDependencies. Commit on `feature/singapore-redesign-v3`. Report back: the screenshot path, a one-paragraph description of the actual creative idea (what makes this hero's composition/motion specific to "Singapore, low-latency APAC VPS" rather than generic), and the commit hash. Keep the report short — this is a fast checkpoint, not a final deliverable.
